name: Play a land on turn 1-2 when nothing in hand unlocks anything
intent: On turn 1 or 2, once none of open-land-unlocks, open-shock-unlocks or open-fetch-unlocks apply and no other hand card is already affordable, still play the land drop - any land in hand beats holding it back with nothing to protect. Prefers a surveil land (Meticulous Archive, Shadowy Backstreet, Undercity Sewers) first, since it was entering tapped regardless and the scry is free value; then any other land that would enter tapped anyway, since playing it now costs no tempo it would not already lose; then a shockland, life declined, since paying for it buys nothing this turn and an idle land drop should not hold a shock back the way F holds a fetch (item 5); then a fetch, held for a target-rich later turn but taken here since nothing else is better. Unlike the other three decks in this pass, the surveil answer bins a big legendary creature (Atraxa, Griselbrand) into the graveyard instead of keeping it - this is instant-reanimator's whole plan: Goryo's Vengeance wants exactly that card in the yard, so an idle turn 1-2 surveil is this deck's own reanimation setup, not lost value. Only turns 1-2, land drop available, mine, precombat main, empty stack. Stands down once the discard outlet (a creature with an own +1/+1-counter-put ability, Psychic Frog in this 60) is already on the battlefield: that fact is byte-identical to the seat-admitted bin-fatty-vs-permanent-exile play's own battlefield-outlet true key, and it can never hold on a genuine turn 1-2 board anyway - the outlet costs two mana and has to survive a turn cycle before that play reads it as safe to fire, so this key costs this play nothing here and only prevents the two plays overlapping later in the game.
